title: Ryobi 18V ONE+ HP Brushless Drill & Drive 2Ah Kit $199 Delivered / C&C / in-Store @ Bunnings Warehouse
body:
Deal: Ryobi 18V ONE+ HP Brushless Drill & Drive 2Ah Kit $199 Delivered / C&C / in-Store @ Bunnings Warehouse

[drillvoice] I have this drill and this driver and I rate them both.
[muzeeb] Ditto - they punch above their budget weight
[ifreddo] Same. Can't fault them. So compact but good grunt.
[vid_ghost] Are these better then the Bosch Home & Garden 18V 2 Piece Easy Kit: Drill/Driver, Impact Driver, 2 x 2.5Ah Batteries and 3.0Ah Fast Charger Set for $239?
Extra $40 gets you 2x larger batteries. vs 1x smaller batter on the Ryobi set
[Nom] Bosch Green gear is very basic.
This Ryobi kit is significantly better - they're brushless and much more powerful.
[kingmoron] just when i am trying to stray away from ryobi because I lost my original driver … they pull me back. guess I could also use battery adapters on the ryobi
[bogak] I have this kit from this deal https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/787086 , it was 2 batteries for that deal. Great drills, still use them today.
[vid_ghost] Bosch Home & Garden 18V 2 Piece Kit still comes with two batteries. I think i will wait for that to go on sale again.
[Nom] See above - that Bosch kit isn't in the same league as this.
If you just want a cheap basic set then stick with Ozito because the warranty is outstanding.
[ploptoilet] Dude stop trying to make the shitty bosch kit happen. It's not gonna happen!
[Leeroy Jenkins] As stated by another commenter, this is league above that Bosch kit you are talking about in terms quality.
A good rule of thumb is, if you see Ryobi HP stuff on sale, you just buy them, unless you're already I'm the Makita/DeWalt/Milwaukee ecosystems.
[rooster7777] forkenell…with 2x 4ah batteries was a great deal!
[georgedn] How much better are these than my ozitos? Genuine question - i need a reason to spend money of this deal
[OldSchoolHarry] Brushless Ozito does everything good enough around the house. I have been using them for last 6 years and very satisfied with them.
[stevtom27] Isnt this the standard price for this bundle. I swear this is commonly available price point
[Wool] I should get the hammer drill kit instead of this for brick walls, right?
[rooster7777] yep…need a hammer drill for brick walls… if you're doing a lot then you'll be better off with good stuff… if you're only doing a single mission or such… get a cheap one and buy this kit as well
[Wool] Cheers, will do some research. Just some basics around the home, including drilling some ikea furniture into a wall. Nothing too exciting.
[OZKap] If you just need to put in small anchors every now and then you'll be able to get away with a hammer drill. If you're putting in big 10+mm anchors or a lot of small ones you'll want an SDS rotary hammer
[jaydee4] Have a look at this Ozito SDS+ Drill (Skin Only/No Battery) from Bunnings. It's very loud so use ear protection. Also get safety glasses and a dust mask.
I used this SDS+ Drill Bit Set from Aliexpress. it's $9 USD when it's on sale.
It's a very efficient setup; goes through brick like butter. Installed 2x wall mounted folding clothlines, 2 sets of door canopies and a new rangehood. It also went through the tile wall just fine(use at your own risk). Used mostly the 10mm and 8mm sds+ bit.
[rbev] Depends on the brick, I've found my old Ryobi one drill driver is fine getting through my brick walls, never need to drag out the hammer drill or the SDS
Just recommend spending a little bit on decent masonry bits.
It's been about 8 years and the clutch is starting to fail so this deal is pretty tempting.
[OZKap] If you're buying this as a starter kit you'll probably want to keep an eye out for another battery too. Having both drill and driver ready to go makes projects a lot smoother
[rooster7777] If only this had come up a few weeks ago… the brushed ozito driver made me work too bloody hard on a big project but prepared now for the next one :)
[bogrolls] I returned a 5 year old ryobi drill at Bunnings on the weekend with little fuss, they swapped it for new. To get your 6 year warranty don’t forget to register shortly after you buy it, while they’re a budget tool I’ve found mine to be fine for home use, I was pushing the drill hard when it cooked but never had a problem before that.
